summary:
Every rating across the board is scorching hot right now, but the signal to trust is narrow: it's the same 5-game sample (n=5) repeating identically across R1 through R4 on trends, runs, sp, bullpen, and hitting — all sitting at 80%. That's not four independent confirmations, it's one slate's worth of results echoing through every rating tier. The real red flag is bullpen_fatigue, which has gone ice cold at 0-5 across all four ratings with a matching 5-game losing streak on every tier. Season-long, bullpen_fatigue sits at just 45-47% anyway, so fading it isn't new — but a 0-for-5 across the board this deep into November means any pick leaning on bullpen_fatigue as a tiebreaker should be downgraded hard today, while sp (3W streak on every rating, 52-55% season) and trends (56-59% season, the best-performing category by far) deserve the benefit of the doubt.

For tonight's board, lean into the trends+sp combo specifically — it's the top category pairing all year at 58% (370-268, n=638) and both categories are riding the same 3W/80% hot streak simultaneously, which is the strongest convergence signal available. R4's strong-play tier is the one to watch for value: its season strong-play number is a elite 64% (+63.0u, n=187), the best win-rate of any rating, even though its 30-day strong window cooled to 50% (-1.0u, n=6) — the 14-day bounce-back to 3-1 (+1.0u) suggests that cold patch is over. If tonight's slate includes MIL, TBR, BOS, or LAD, give those picks extra weight regardless of rating — LAD is money when liked (80% strong, +27.0u) and BOS's strong-play number (76%, +19.0u) is right behind it. Conversely, treat any NYY pick with suspicion; the model is a coinflip on them generally (49%) and actively bleeds when strong-rated (39%, -4.0u) — that's the one team-level fade worth flagging against tonight's board.
